contract: A logical write has a maximum of three physical send attempts across both gateway retries and transport retries. A token is consumed before every send, including timed-out sends; there is no token refund for an unknown outcome.

evidenceRequirements.description: Establish any valid causal witness from the supplied code and context; exact driver numbers/order are not required. One evaluator-only witness: The gateway retries once after the transport consumes three tokens. A fresh token object on re-entry permits three more physical sends (six total); the request-owned object permits only three. A timeout does not establish that a send did not occur.

Explain at least one relevant boundary or benign path inferable from the supplied code/context; the following evaluator examples are alternatives, not a mandatory unseen checklist: First-send success consumes one token; success on the third consumes three; an ambiguous final timeout consumes its token and the gateway cannot replenish it.
The retry budget scope: is three a logical-write cap or a per-transport-invocation cap?

Under this contract: A logical write has a maximum of three physical send attempts across both gateway retries and transport retries. A token is consumed before every send, including timed-out sends; there is no token refund for an unknown outcome. the traced behavior is a defect. Alternative: If three is only a per-transport-invocation cap and two gateway invocations are permitted, six sends obey the supplied local retry rule; no logical-write cap has been established.

forbiddenClaims: Production outage, real data exfiltration or universal safety without supplied evidence.
A missing contract establishes either a definite defect or unconditional protection.
Simulated time or offline passing tests establish real scheduler/OS behavior or model improvement.
independence: non-independent, same-workflow authorship and public artifacts
